thread:
acme_dev: Hey team — getting a 400 from embeddings API intermittently when sending batches from our Node worker. Started after we switched to streaming upload.
acme_dev: payload is ndjson (each line is a JSON object with {\"input\": \"...\"}). sometimes succeeds, sometimes returns \"invalid input shape\" and downstream vector index shows dim 0 entries.
zoe_support: thanks — can you paste a redacted example of one of the failing lines? and your Content-Type header?
acme_dev: sure — Content-Type: application/x-ndjson
acme_dev: example line: {"input": ["customer note 1"], "meta": {"id":"row-42"}}
acme_dev: worker sends ~1000 lines in a single POST stream. first few chunks succeed then we see a burst of 400s.
zoe_support: hmm. NDJSON should work but we expect top-level object with input as string or array of strings for the batch endpoint. streaming NDJSON is supported but each line must be exactly the per-request schema. any chance some lines are arrays-of-arrays (e.g., pre-tokenized or client mistakenly serializing buffers)?
matt_eng: jumping in — this looks like a shape/encoding flake. very common: some of your worker threads are serializing req.body as JSON.stringify([line]) (wrapping the line again) which yields nested arrays for input when you intended a single item. that will produce inconsistent shapes per-line.
acme_dev: oh! we do have a helper that conditionally wraps if batchSize===1. might be the culprit.
zoe_support: can you grep logs for "[[" occurrences in the stream or look for Content-Length spikes? also check if any lines are empty (CRLF only) — those get parsed as empty JSON by some parsers.
acme_dev: repro steps I tried locally:
```
# bad: node worker accidentally double-wrapping
const line = JSON.stringify({ input: ["note"] });
stream.write(JSON.stringify(line) + "\n"); // -> "\"{\\\"input\\\":[\\\"note\\\"]}\"" as a JSON string line
```
This produces the server error: 400 invalid input shape (expected array of strings).

# good fix
stream.write(JSON.stringify({ input: ["note"] }) + "\n");
# and set Content-Type: application/x-ndjson
```
acme_dev: after removing the accidental JSON.stringify wrapper, failures disappeared locally. production still had a few fails though.
zoe_support: did you also mix in plain JSON array payloads with the ndjson stream? the server treats the entire request differently if the initial bytes look like '[' (it will parse array-of-objects instead of NDJSON). mixing both clients to the same endpoint at high throughput can hit edge cases at the ingress if chunk boundaries align oddly.
acme_dev: we did have a backup path that posts a single JSON array for small batches. maybe concurrent sends collided.
matt_eng: two practical recommendations: 1) standardize on one content type per job (prefer application/x-ndjson for streaming) 2) add a quick validation step on producer side: ensure typeof line.input === 'string' || (Array.isArray(line.input) && typeof line.input[0] === 'string') before writing. also add an incrementing batch-id header so you can correlate ingested lines on the server side.
acme_dev: thanks — we'll roll these checks. question: can the API return a 422 with more detail instead of a generic 400 so we can alert faster?
zoe_support: good ask. I'll file an internal ticket to improve error messages for shape mismatches (more explicit: \"unexpected nested array at input[0]\"). tagging @ingest-bot to track.
ingest-bot: ticket created: IN-4921 - Improve embeddings API error for nested input arrays. Priority: P3.
acme_dev: awesome, thanks. one last thing — we saw some embeddings with length 0 vectors in our index after failures; any chance partial writes happen?
matt_eng: partial writes shouldn't occur on 400; however if your downstream index ingester consumes from a queue that wasn't atomic with request success, you could see empty vectors. check your consumer that converts API responses to index upserts. also verify you aren't dropping/rewriting the vector field when parsing error payloads.
acme_dev: will audit that. appreciate the help, saved us hours. :tada:
